clips.send: Absolute advantage. Making MORE of something with the same resources. Peach Isle catches 6 fish an hour; Bamboo Isle catches 1. Peach Isle has the absolute advantage in fish. Peach Isle also gathers more coconuts per hour (3 vs 2) — it has the absolute advantage in BOTH goods. Surprise: trade can still help both islands. Absolute advantage is not what decides who should make what.

clips.send: Trade barriers. Government actions that limit trade: tariffs, quotas, embargoes. A tariff is a tax on imports. Buyers at home usually end up paying higher prices. A quota limits the quantity of an import. An embargo bans trade with a country. Barriers can protect some home jobs and raise money — but they raise prices and invite retaliation. Trade agreements (USMCA, the EU’s single market, WTO rules) lower barriers between members.

clips.send: Comparative advantage. Making something at a LOWER opportunity cost than others. On Peach Isle, 1 coconut costs 2 fish (the hour could have caught 6 fish instead of 3 coconuts). On Bamboo Isle, 1 coconut costs only ½ fish. Bamboo Isle has the comparative advantage in coconuts. Peach Isle has the comparative advantage in fish (1 fish costs ½ coconut there, but 2 coconuts on Bamboo Isle). When each specializes in its comparative advantage and trades, total output rises.

clips.send: Specialization and voluntary trade. Each side focuses on what it does best — then both trade freely. Voluntary trade happens only when both sides expect to gain — or one would walk away. Georgia specializes too: poultry, peanuts, carpets from Dalton, Gulfstream jets from Savannah. Specialization makes trade necessary: a country that makes lots of one thing must trade for the rest.

clips.send: Exchange rate. The price of one currency in terms of another. In 2024, $1 bought about ¥7.20 on average (World Bank). Most currencies move with supply and demand; China manages the yuan within a range. A stronger yuan makes Chinese exports pricier abroad and foreign trips cheaper for Chinese families.

clips.send: 汇率。一种货币用另一种货币表示的价格。 2024 年，平均 1 美元约兑换 7.20 元人民币（世界银行）。 大多数货币随供求变动；中国在一定范围内对人民币汇率进行管理。 人民币升值，中国出口商品在国外变贵，中国家庭出国旅游变便宜。

clips.send: 比较优势。以比别人更低的机会成本生产某种商品。 在蜜桃岛，1 个椰子的代价是 2 条鱼（一小时可以捕 6 条鱼，也可以采 3 个椰子）。 在竹子岛，1 个椰子只要 ½ 条鱼。竹子岛在椰子上有比较优势。 蜜桃岛在捕鱼上有比较优势（在那里 1 条鱼只要 ½ 个椰子，在竹子岛要 2 个椰子）。 各自专门生产有比较优势的商品再交换，总产量就会增加。

clips.send: 绝对优势。用同样的资源生产得更多。 蜜桃岛每小时捕 6 条鱼，竹子岛只捕 1 条。蜜桃岛在捕鱼上有绝对优势。 蜜桃岛每小时采的椰子也更多（3 对 2）——它在两种商品上都有绝对优势。 出乎意料：贸易仍然能让两座岛都受益。决定谁生产什么的，并不是绝对优势。

clips.send: 贸易壁垒。限制贸易的政府措施：关税、配额、禁运。 关税是对进口商品征收的税，最终通常由国内买家以更高的价格承担。 配额限制进口商品的数量；禁运则禁止与某国贸易。 壁垒可以保护部分国内就业、增加政府收入——但会抬高价格，还可能招致报复。 贸易协定（美墨加协定、欧盟统一市场、世贸组织规则）降低成员之间的壁垒。

clips.send: 专业化与自愿交易。各自专注于最擅长的事，再自由交换。 只有双方都预期能获益时，自愿交易才会发生——否则一方会走开。 佐治亚州也搞专业化：禽肉、花生、多尔顿的地毯、萨凡纳的湾流公务机。 专业化使贸易成为必需：大量生产一种东西的国家，必须用它去换别的东西。
